title: Circuit-breaker telemetry inventory and weekly huddle notes — 2028-08-14
body:
Summary

This week’s huddle focused on the circuit-breaker telemetry inventory (a small cross-functional spike to map what signals we have vs. what we need to trigger graceful degradation), short-term dashboard changes to surface circuit tripping, and a cost telemetry probe for span amplification from fanout paths. The goal: reduce noisy alerts, increase signal precision for automated fallback, and get a first-pass cost model for enabling adaptive sampling on busy endpoints.

Attendees

Priya (notetaker), Marco, Sana, Ethan, Leah, and guests from platform (Juno) and serving-runtime (Ravi).

Agenda and decisions

1) Circuit-breaker signals inventory
- Reviewed current signals: error-rate (5xx per 1m), p50/p95 latency, token-lag (queue wait estimate), and CPU/GPU utilization per pool.
- Found gaps: no per-route prefix-based amplification metric (we only have model-level request counts), and KV-cache eviction rate is not instrumented in the agent.
- Decision: implement a lightweight amplification counter in the router (per-route fanout multiplier) and expose as a taggable metric for tracing spans. Spike owner: Marco, ETA: 2028-08-21.

2) Dashboard surface changes (quick wins)
- Add a new dashboard row: "Circuit-breaker health" showing per-region tripped-rate, recent fallbacks, and last-triggered rule. This is a temporary per-route table linked from the main latency dashboard. Task owner: Leah.
- Add an alert suppression window for noisy model warmup failures (observed at autoscale events). Dev note: use 10m suppression with exponential backoff for the same route. Ticket: JIRA:OBS-2197.

3) Cost telemetry probe: span amplification
- Problem: several heavy routes fan out to scoring pipelines and external pre/post processors; end-to-end spans multiply and balloon storage and ingestion costs. Last month we saw a 18% increase in trace ingestion for the "rerank-multistage" pipeline.
- Action: run a 2-week probe to compute amplification factor per route: (total child-spans / request) and estimate storage impact. Sana + Ethan to run the probe and deliver a cost delta estimate by 2028-08-28.

4) Sampling and retention policy options
- Options discussed: adaptive sampling per-route (priority on high-cost, low-value traces), TTL-based retention with cheap cold storage for long tails, and dynamic snapshotting for anomalies.
- Quick decision: enable conservative adaptive sampling on rerank-multistage with a 1% sample baseline for high-throughput routes, increase to 10% when anomaly score > threshold. Implementation owner: Ethan. Safety measure: keep a rolling 24h 100% capture for any route with a circuit trip.

Operational notes and quick wins

- Runbook update: added a short section for "circuit breaker chasing"—how to identify if a fallback was triggered by capacity vs. a model-level error. Placeholder link in runbook: confluence:observability-circuit-breaker-design.
- Dashboard: added a compact sparkline cell showing tripped-rate over 6h and a link to the trace sample view. Leah will push changes to the dashboard by EOD 2028-08-16.
- Alert tuning: lowered noisy CPU-util alerts on non-production pools; these alerts were causing pager fatigue during batch jobs.

Data and metrics snapshot (from the last 7d prefix view)

- rerank-multistage:
  - avg QPS: 1450
  - observed child-spans per request (sample): 6.2
  - estimated trace bytes/day: 52 GB (post-aggregation)
  - circuit trips: 3 in 7d (two region-specific spikes during cluster upgrades)

- chat-streaming-endpoint:
  - avg QPS: 420
  - child-spans per request: 1.1
  - trace bytes/day: 4 GB
  - circuit trips: 0

Notes: the rerank pipeline is the primary contributor to the ingestion spike; amplification > 5x for certain user flows.

Open questions / risks

- Will per-route amplification counters create excessive tagging cardinality? Plan: only emit amplification metric to metrics backend as a prefixed counter with route-name hashing, not raw route string. Marco will prototype keying strategy.
- Are we confident that a 1% baseline sample will retain enough signal to detect regressions in quality for rerank? We will run an eval on sampled traces against known failure types before flipping adaptive sampling to production.
- Potential downstream: analytics consumers rely on full traces for some post-hoc attributions. We need a migration plan for analytics consumers if retention/sampling changes. Leah will coordinate a consumer impact review.

Action items (owner — due)

- Marco — implement amplification counter in router + prototype tagging key strategy — due 2028-08-21.
- Leah — dashboard row + suppression rule push — due 2028-08-16.
- Sana, Ethan — run probe to compute amplification factor and cost delta — due 2028-08-28.
- Ethan — prototype adaptive sampling controller with circuit-trip override and safe defaults (keep 24h 100% capture on trips) — due 2028-08-25.
- Priya — update runbook with circuit-breaker chasing steps and link to tickets — due 2028-08-18.

Short retrospective from this week

- Good: cross-team presence (platform + serving-runtime) helped surface missing runtime signals quickly. The temporary dashboard approach is low friction and should materially improve ops response time.
- Bad: we still surface too many low-fidelity alerts during infra deploys; suppression windows and better tagging should help but need engineering work.
- Weird: an odd spike in child-span counts correlated with a canary that added a synchronous enrichment call; we need to confirm whether the enrichment call uses streaming or batched RPCs.

Meeting log snippets / adhoc notes

- Marco: "If we can key on hashed prefix rather than route name we can keep downstream cardinality manageable and still find top amplifiers."
- Sana: "We should baseline costs by user-flow rather than route — some flows fan out more, but are rare."
- Ethan: "Adaptive sampling needs a safety net; don't let sampling make debug impossible when a regression starts."

Relevant links & references

- OBS probe dashboard (temp): dashboard://obs/probes/circuit-breaker-amplification
- Trace cost runbook fragment: confluence:trace-costs-2028
- PR to infra router (amplification counter): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1432
- Tickets: JIRA:OBS-2183 (circuit-breaker inventory) and JIRA:OBS-2197 (dashboard suppression).

Next meeting

- Quick Sync: 2028-08-21 10:00 PT — focus: prototype review (Marco), dashboard preview (Leah), probe status (Sana/Ethan).

Notes to self

- Keep an eye on the rerank probe for this weekend; schedule a brief on-call rotation so someone can respond if the sampling controller misfires.
- Consider a follow-up spike to instrument KV-cache eviction if the amplification probe still shows the rerank pipeline as dominant contributor.

End of notes.
